name: UWF Rampage Championship
caption: A singles championship contested on the wing's own weekly broadcasts, held by Paul Wong entering this pass's own August 2003 record.
epitaph: Defended nearly every week on Saturday Night Rampage, with Paul Wong retaining it against Tom Landis on 9 August 2003 after Team Canada's interference disqualified the challenger.

name: UWF Cruiserweight Championship of the World
caption: A singles championship for the wing's lighter-weight division, changing hands twice inside three weeks in the wing's own 2003 record.
epitaph: Won by Uriah Hawkins at Gold Rush 2003 and lost in his first defense two and a half weeks later to a same-night replacement challenger, Chris O'Brien, after Hawkins broke his arm on a botched moonsault fall.

name: UWF World Tag Team Championship
caption: The wing's top tag team championship, held by the Ghost Dancers entering this pass's own August 2003 record.
epitaph: Held by the Ghost Dancers, Jason and Michael Keening, who retained it by default on 9 August 2003 when a three-way defense against Team Canada and Alex Extreme and Quinn Brown was thrown out as a no-contest.

name: UWF North American Heavyweight Championship
caption: A singles championship held by Eugene Robinson entering this pass's own August 2003 record.
epitaph: Defended to a draw by Eugene Robinson against Tragedy on 30 August 2003 after Derek Irvin's outside interference forced a double stoppage.

name: UWF Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World
caption: The wing's women's championship, won by Stephanie Harper at Gold Rush 2003 and defended against three different challengers within this pass's own record.
epitaph: Won by Stephanie Harper at Gold Rush 2003 and retained against Bliss on 30 August 2003, with a three-way defense against Nina Grimsson and Myra Benedict promised for the following week after their own title-eliminator ended in a draw.

name: UWF Heavyweight Championship of the World
caption: The wing's top singles championship, held by Edmond Winston IV entering this pass's own October 2003 record.
epitaph: Retained by Edmond Winston IV over "Doctor EMS" Eric Matthew Somers on 4 October 2003 under a stipulation that ended Somers's own UWF career.

name: UWF North American Tag Team Championship
caption: A tag team championship held by Team Canada entering this pass's own October 2003 record, until the Ghost Dancers exploited a fine-print contract clause to win it alone.
epitaph: Won by the Ghost Dancers from Team Canada with stereo scorpion deathlocks on 25 October 2003, after a contract clause meant only this title, not the World Tag Team Championship, was actually on the line in the match.

name: UWF Women's Tag Team Championship
caption: A women's tag team championship billed as held by the Love Sisters, Leanna and Lolita Love, entering this pass's own October 2003 record.
epitaph: Held by the Love Sisters, Leanna and Lolita, whom the promotion's own broadcast names as champions; not defended in their 22 October 2003 six-person loss to the Coven, a three-on-three match with no title match of its own.

name: UWF Meltdown Championship
caption: A singles championship for the wing's own midweek program, crowned in a fifteen-man battle royal and two-match tournament on the show's first-ever title edition.
epitaph: Commissioner Becky Byers announced the title the week before, framing it as ending Meltdown's own status as a secondary program; Papa Legba won the inaugural tournament on 17 December 2003, beating Paul Wong in the finals with the Black Magic superbomb.

name: UWF Eurasian Heavyweight Championship
caption: A singles championship for the UWF-Eurasia roster, defended on the flagship Meltdown card for the first time by Colby Greene.
epitaph: Colby Greene, already champion, retained over "The Hero" Marcus Johnson by pinfall (the Bayou Bomb) on the belt's own first defense on the flagship Meltdown card, 20 October 2004.

name: UWF Unified Television Championship
caption: A singles championship created by unifying the Meltdown and Rampage Championships, held by Marcus Nuit as its first champion.
epitaph: Marcus Nuit, the reigning Rampage Champion, beat Meltdown Champion Tigress by pinfall (the 51st Drop) in a title unification match on 22 June 2005 to become the belt's first champion, then retained it by disqualification over "Violent" Victor Frost in its own first defense on 6 July 2005 after Sabbath's own interference.

name: UWF Women's North American Championship
caption: A second women's title alongside the long-running Women's Heavyweight Championship of the World, its first champion already crowned by the time of this record.
epitaph: Instituted as a second tier for the women's division, with Sonya Benedict billed as its first champion and a twenty-second countout rule set for her own title defenses.
